To: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Appeals Department  
[Appeals mailing address, fax number, or portal identified by Anthem Member Services]

Date: [Date sent]

Re: Expedited reconsideration request for CPT 63030  
Member: Taylor Alvarez  
Member ID: W709290584  
Reference number: POC-A43FE266AD-51849  
Notice date: August 21, 2026  
Requested service: Lumbar disc surgery/decompression

Dear Anthem Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lumbar decompression with treatment of the L4-L5 disc extrusion. The appeal deadline stated in the notice is February 17, 2027.

The clinical record directly addresses the stated concern regarding whether the imaging supports medical necessity. The June 9, 2026 lumbar MRI shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion causing severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root. This is an objective structural abnormality at a specific spinal level that corresponds to Taylor Alvarez’s clinical findings.

The imaging is consistent with the patient’s symptoms and examination:

- Taylor has experienced progressive lower-back pain for 14 months, unrelieved by rest.
- Taylor has radicular pain extending into the right calf.
- Taylor cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side.
- A neurologic deficit was documented that corresponds to the imaged level and affected nerve root.
- The MRI demonstrates severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root at L4-L5.

The patient has also completed substantial nonoperative treatment without adequate improvement:

- Twenty supervised physical-therapy visits over 12 weeks, from April 4 through June 27, 2026, including core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility treatment.
- Eight months of NSAID treatment with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 3, 2026, producing only two weeks of partial relief.

The combination of persistent and function-limiting radicular symptoms, a corresponding neurologic deficit, failure of prolonged conservative care, and MRI-confirmed L5 nerve-root compression supports reconsideration of the requested decompression. The requested procedure is directed at the documented L4-L5 pathology rather than nonspecific low-back pain alone.

The record also documents the absence of the following complicating factors:

- No active infection.
- No untreated substance-use disorder.
- BMI 29.
- Nonsmoker.

Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgeon, has submitted the request and can provide any additional clinical information, imaging review, or peer-to-peer discussion needed.

I request that Anthem reverse the denial and approve CPT 63030. If Anthem maintains the denial, please provide the specific medical policy or clinical-utilization guideline, version, effective date, and exact criteria applied to this request, including any vendor criteria used in the review. The public materials I located did not establish which specific Indiana commercial/ACA policy or criteria governed this determination, so this appeal does not quote or assume any unverified plan policy language.

Please also provide the complete clinical-review rationale explaining why the June 9 MRI was considered insufficient despite the documented L4-L5 disc extrusion, severe right lateral recess stenosis, traversing L5 nerve-root compression, corresponding neurologic deficit, and failure of conservative treatment.

Sincerely,

Taylor Alvarez  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Authorized representative, if applicable: [Name and relationship]  
Enclosures: MRI report dated June 9, 2026; physical-therapy discharge note; medication and injection records; examination findings; surgeon’s prior-authorization submission.
